6. In order to reach at a just conclusion, we deem it appropriate to mention here that Section 20 of thc Offcnccs Against Propcrty (Enforcement ./ of IJudood) Ordinance 1979 clcarly provides punishment for Ilaraabah liable to 'ladzir.

For advantageous purpose Section 20 of the Ordinance is rcproduced bclow:- "20. Punishment for haraabah liuble to tuzir. Whoever commils haraabah which is not liable to the punishment provided fitr in seclion 17, or for which proof in either of the forms mentioned in section 7 is nol available, or for which punishment of amPutation or dealh may not be imposed or enforced under this Ordinance, shall be awarded, the punishment provided in the Pakistan Penal Code (Act XLV of 1860)

From thc abovo quoted provision it has becomc clearer than crystal that if an accused is tried under Ifudood Ordinance, even thcn he can be punished under 'lahzir.

Besidcs, the question involved in this and in thc conncctcd appcal had carlicr bcen brought bclbrc the llon'ble Federal Shariat Court in the casc of "Iiazal Din Vs. Tai Din" rcported as PLD 1983 FSC 33 whcrein it had elaborately becn discussed / decided in the Ibllowing tcrms: - "r/ "The offence under Seclion 302 PPC is certainly an offence under a law other than the Ordinance but the Sessions Judge being competent to try both the offence with which the respondenl is charged, he could pass a sentences in a case tried by him under the Ordinance for an offence under the PPC also.

What he could do can also be compelently done by an aPPellate court. Now proviso 2 of subsection (l) of Section 20 provides that "an offince punishable under this Ordinance shall be triable by a court of Session" and an appeal .fro* an order of the Court of Session shall lie to the Federal Shariat Courl. Proviso I of the same subsection permits lhe competent court (Sessions Judge in lhe present case) to try the offince under any other law also and award punishment thereunder. By virtue of this provision the trial and conviction by the Sessions Judge of any offince inter alia under the PPC becomes an offence punishable under this Ordinance for the purpose of appeal to lhe Federal Shariat Court. This can e the onlY reasonable interpretation of the two provisos of section (20) of the Ordinance. For convcnient we would like to rcproducc Section 24 of the Ordinancc ibid, which rcads as undcr: - "24. Applicution of Code of Criminol Procedure, 1598.-(l) The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, l89B (Act V oJ' lB9B), shall apply, mutatis mutandis, in respecl of cases under this Ordinance:

I'rovided that, if il appears in evidence that the offender has committed o c dffirent offence under anY olher law, he may, if the Court is competent to try that offence and to award punishment therefore, he convicted and punished for that offence,' Provided .furlher thal an offence punishable under section 9 or section 17 shall be triable bY a Court of Session and not by a Magistrate authorised under section 30 of the said Code and an appeal ,from an order under either of the said sections, i or from an order under any provision of this Ordinance which imPose a sentence of imprisonmenl for a term exceeding two years, shall lie to the Federal Shariat Court,' Provided furlher lhat a trial by a Court of Session under this Ordinance shall ordinarily be held at the headquarters of the Tehsil in which lhe offence is alleged to have been committed.

A glance over proviso (2) to Section 24 clearly dcpicted that punishrncnt exceeding two (02) years shall lie to the Ifon'ble Federal Shariat Court. Reliance in this respcct may also be placed on the judgment dclivcrcd by I{on'ble Shariat Appcllate Jurisdiction delivercd in the case of "Muhammad Sh Vs. The State" reported as PLD 1999 SC 1063 where it was held as under: oNf "We have given serious thought to the submissions of lhe learner c'ounsel for the parties and have also minutelY gone through the aforenoted judgments and the relevant provisions contained in four Hudood Laws i.e Offence of Zina (Effircement of Iludood) Ordinance, 1979 (Ordinance WI of 1979), (ffince of Qarf (Enforcement of l{add) Ordinance, 1979 (Ordinance VIII of 1979), the Prohibition Order (President's Order No.4 o.f 1979) and under the Offences against Property (Enforcement of Hudood) Ordinance, 1979 (Ordinance VI of 1979). A close study of the history of these four lludood Law and the amendments introduced therein from time to time show that when the Prohibition Order as well as Ordinance VI of 1979 relating to Offences against Property were promulgated in 1979, provisions of section 24 of Ordinance 1979 and Article 27 of the Prohibition Order contemplated trial of the offence by ordinary criminal Courts and the appeals to be heard and decided by the forum provided by the Code of Criminal Procedure. Both these provisions provide that unless otherwise provided, the provisions of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 shall apply mutatis mulandis in respect of cases under the Ordinance/Order. In 1980 Federal Shariat Court was established and vide Presidential Order No.5 of l9B0 second proviso was added to Article 27 of the Prohibition Order (P.O. No.4 of 1979) and vide Ordinance No.XIX of 1979 (second proviso was added in section 24 of Ordinance No.VI of 1979 relating to Offences against Property whereby offinces punishable under Article B of the Prohibilion Order and the offinces punishable under section 9 or section 17 of Ordinance No.VI of 1979 (Offences against Property) were made triable exclusively by a Sessions Court; and orders passed under the said Article/sections were made appealable before the Federal Shariat Court. " It is also to be borne in mind that proviso9 o,rd (2) to Section 24 of the Offences Against Property (Enforcement of Hudood) Ordinance, 1979 provides that the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 shall apply mutatis mutandis, poses no difficulty in preferring the aforenoted interpretation.
